lifeplan / full factorial sweep / example

1,176 ways this household could go

Five axes, every combination, each one a complete plan run to the year the earner turns 100. The answer spreads from −1.78 to +4.43 hundred-million yen. The point of running all of them is not to count how many fail — that number says more about which scenarios were put in than about the household — but to see which axis moves the answer. The household is invented — see the caveat at the foot.

1,176cells, each a full plan
50%of the spread is where the household lives
94.7%of the spread explained by the five axes alone
160cells turned the home into cash

What was varied

One decision per axis. The first level of every axis is the plan as written

A bundle like "carry on as now" moves several things at once, so a row of results can only say which bundle was chosen — never which dial did the work. Splitting the bundles into one decision per axis and running the full product answers that.

How wide it spreads

Net worth in the final year, in today's prices, hundred-million yen

Assets stop at zero and never go negative. A plan that cannot pay records the amount it could not pay as a shortfall and carries on. Read straight, every ruined cell would sit at zero and the measure would go flat exactly where it matters most. So the response is assets less cumulative shortfall, which can go negative.

What actually moves it

Variance explained, η². The share of the spread each axis accounts for

A balanced full factorial lets the spread be split cleanly by axis. This is the most honest measure of sensitivity — moving one factor at a time gives a different answer depending on where the others were parked.

The economy is not a choice

Fixing the economy, then swinging every dial from best to worst

In the harshest economies every combination fails. No setting of the dials keeps this household solvent there. That is the sweep's most useful output: it says plainly where the problem is not something the household can fix by choosing differently.

The dials, one at a time

Median net worth and ruin rate for each level

Housing against living cost

Every other axis swept inside each square

The home is the last thing left

When a plan cannot pay, it either sells and rents, or borrows against the house

Both measures need the mortgage repaid first: a house already pledged cannot be pledged again, and selling means clearing the loan out of the proceeds. The plan builds both and takes whichever is better — it is not a choice the household makes.

What this does not answer

How likely ruin is. 630 of the 1,176 combinations fail, which is 53.6% of them — and that figure means nothing on its own. It is the share of the scenarios that were put in, not a probability: load the sweep with pessimistic economies and it rises, load it with optimistic ones and it falls. Nobody can grade the scenarios accurately enough for the share to become a chance. The seven economies and the seven crashes here are counted equally, and they are not equally likely. Read the axes, not the count.

Asset allocation by age. Contributions are fixed to one execution policy; nothing here varies the mix of shares and bonds. Knowing that a crash hurts most just before drawdown does not tell you what to do about it.

Care, redundancy, inheritance. None of them is an axis.

Anything about a real household. Every figure describes an invented one.

Generated by tools/sweep, which passes overrides to plan.Build rather than writing 1,176 manifests. Results in out/sweep/cells.tsv. Reproduce with go run ./tools/sweep && python3 examples/analyse.py && python3 examples/build.py.

The household in this report does not exist. Nobody lives at these figures. But they are not invented either: the pay comes from the 民間給与実態統計調査 by age band, the spouse's from the 賃金構造基本統計調査 hourly rate for part-time women, the spending from the 家計調査 for the head's age band, and the rent and the price from the going rate for a 70㎡ flat in 八王子市. Each one is cited in data/controllable/README.md. The dial choices, the statutory rules and the economic projections are real; only the household is not. Amounts are real terms, discounted to the plan's first year. Pension levels follow the 2024 財政検証; the crash severity is a chosen round figure, not a property of any particular portfolio.
